statement.en: Read a line of a song in kana, with the romaji switched off, and type it back
statement.es: Leer una línea de canción en kana, con el romaji apagado, y escribirla de vuelta

note.en: No source in the research supports songs as a confidence device, and none refutes it either. This chapter is a judgment call, labelled as one.

title.en: Nineteen songs, and why not twenty

unlocks.en: real Japanese sentences that repeat, rhyme and stay in your head, at a point where nothing else can

title.en: A song is the first text that repeats itself on purpose

en: After chapter 1 you can decode kana and you know almost no words. A song is the one kind of text where that is enough: the lines are short, the vocabulary repeats, and you already have a tune to hang it on.

Be warned that this is a judgment rather than a finding. The research looked for evidence that songs build early confidence and found none either way. What the guides actually use are dice, timers and a first hundred words.

title.en: Why the list is exactly nineteen

en: Song lyrics are copyrighted, and a childhood song being famous is not the same as it being free. Twenty-four candidates were checked against two different laws. Nineteen are out of copyright in Japan and in the United States, and those nineteen are the whole of what this site carries.

Five failed. Two have lyricists who died in the 1970s, so they stay under Japanese copyright until 2043 and 2046. One was restored in the United States by a treaty. One is a wartime rewrite of a song whose original text is fine, and the original is what ships. One is a single verse of a song whose other two verses are clear.

None of the five appears anywhere in this project, including in a comment. A checker in tools/ fails the build if one ever does, and it does not spell the titles out either, because a detector that wrote them down would be the first thing to break its own rule.

title.en: The judgment travels with the data

en: Every song file carries its own verdict for each country, the basis for it, and a confidence level. One of the nineteen is medium-high rather than high for the United States, and the file says so and says why: its verdict rests on a 1927 publication date, and a later one would restore it until 2027.
That is recorded next to the lyrics rather than in a spreadsheet somebody has to remember to check.

unlocks.en: reading kana in a line rather than a character at a time

en: Kana is always shown. Romaji and the English are behind switches, and both begin turned off, because a romaji line the eye can reach is a romaji line the eye reads.
Turn them on when you are stuck. Turn them off before you go again.

The speak button uses the voice built into your browser. It is synthetic and it is not a singer, so treat it as a pronunciation check and not as a recording. If your browser has no Japanese voice, the line says so rather than doing nothing.

title.en: Pick a song and read it

unlocks.en: the chapter goal. Reading a line back is what proves the kana is yours.

en: You are shown a line in kana with its English, and you type it back: read each kana, type its sound in romaji, and the box turns it into hiragana as you go. The romaji of the line is behind a Hint button, and using it is recorded. Spaces and punctuation are ignored when it is marked, because the printed sources break the lines differently from each other.
The eight songs offered here are the ones with the shortest lines. Ten kana is a reasonable first line to type. Twenty-seven is not, and one of the nineteen has a line that long.

title.en: Type the line back in kana
Put the line back in order

unlocks.en: reading a line as a sequence of words rather than a wall of kana, on all nineteen songs and not only the short ones
unlocks.es: leer un verso como una secuencia de palabras y no como un muro de kana, en las diecinueve canciones y no solo en las cortas

title.en: The pieces are given, the order is not
title.es: Las piezas te las dan, el orden no

en: A line arrives cut into its words and shuffled, and you put it back. Typing asks you to produce every kana; this asks only where each piece goes, so it works on the long lines that the typing drill had to leave out. All nineteen songs are here, not the eight with the shortest lines.

Each song is one round, and each round is a game from quiz.neorgon.com running inside a frame on this page. Answers are recorded here under this chapter's goal, and beside every frame there is an Open in Quiz link that opens the same round on its own page.
The English meaning is shown after a miss and on the results screen, never before one. Guessing a line from its meaning is not reading it.
es: Un verso llega cortado en sus palabras y mezclado, y tú lo recompones. Escribir te pide producir cada kana; esto solo pregunta dónde va cada pieza, así que funciona con los versos largos que el ejercicio de escritura tuvo que dejar fuera. Están las diecinueve canciones, no las ocho de versos más cortos.

Cada canción es una ronda, y cada ronda es un juego de quiz.neorgon.com que se ejecuta dentro de un marco en esta página. Las respuestas se registran aquí bajo la meta de este capítulo, y junto a cada marco hay un enlace Abrir en Quiz que abre la misma ronda en su propia página.
El significado en inglés se muestra tras un fallo y en la pantalla de resultados, nunca antes. Adivinar un verso por su significado no es leerlo.

unlocks.en: the only material anyone actually keeps studying: the thing they were going to listen to anyway

title.en: Paste the song you are actually listening to

en: Nineteen public-domain songs is a small shelf, and none of them is what is in your headphones. So paste what is.

It stays in this browser. It is never uploaded, it is never put into a link, and it is not included when you sign in and sync. The database on the other side has no table for it, which is a design decision rather than an oversight.
That is not a privacy flourish. Lyrics you paste are somebody else's copyright, and the only version of this feature that is clearly lawful is the one where the text never leaves your machine.
